WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 of seller_payouts_reserves_chargebacks (category payout), scenario env_0054_ecommerce_marketplace_operator. Round 2 (rework after audits/policy_task/seller_payouts_reserves_chargebacks/_difficulty.md, 0.md, 1.md); every figure below is recomputed on the round-2 world.

[Step 0 — draw and scope] draw_counts.py --task 0 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [5, 5, 6, 6]}. Assignment: root payout_ext_on_demand_payout 6 factors, payout_ext_instant_fee_posting 6, payout_ext_scheduled_payout_limit 5, payout_ext_won_chargeback_debit_return 5. Claimed here: four extended policies on payout_disbursement (scheduled and on-demand), payout_instant_fee and payout_chargeback_reversal (debit component); tools send_scheduled_payout_7857f918 (agent), return_won_chargeback_debit_b5e77014 (agent), post_instant_payout_fee_64da22a6 (agent), request_on_demand_payout_667d53e6 (user). Task 1 holds the other two policies (card settlement of a negative balance, fee component of a won chargeback). A reserve release books exactly the reserve placed, once per order and reserve type, so it carries no computable variation and is not claimed as a problem.

[Why this is a good test] The seller asks for an on-demand payout of what is available today; the dashboard figure (payable 45,325.05) is not what may go out. The on-demand rule states three prerequisite sentences — fixed only after the day's scheduled payout stands on the ledger; not worked out until every won chargeback case carries its returned debit; worked out only once every instant payout sent that day carries its fee — and all three are false at the opening. The agent must find the policy that brings each state about, compute three amounts (5-6 factors each, over ledger history and three other products), book them, then compute the on-demand amount on the changed world.

[Problem tree] root payout_ext_on_demand_payout (user). Edges, all value_input on payable_now, form state:
 (1) <- scheduled payout. Sentence: "An on-demand payout is fixed only after the scheduled payout due on the same payout day stands on the payments ledger." Opening: Payments Daily Plus pays every business day; 2026-10-15 is a Thursday, not a federal holiday; the latest scheduled payout entry is dated 2026-10-02. Only send_scheduled_payout_7857f918 books payout_method scheduled. Skip-run: on-demand 38,957.96.
 (2) <- won chargeback debit return. Sentence (negated direction): "An on-demand payout is not worked out until every chargeback case whose dispute is recorded as won carries its returned-debit entry on the payments ledger." Opening: dispute 2026-09-09 on CB-20260908-2264 won; debit 2,860.00 of 2026-09-08; no reversal entry. Only return_won_chargeback_debit_b5e77014 books debit_returned. Skip-run: 5,944.81.
 (3) <- instant fee. Sentence: "Before an on-demand payout amount is worked out, every instant payout already sent that day must carry its instant payout fee entry on the payments ledger." Opening: instant payout IP-20261015-527 of 4,800.00 dated 2026-10-15 without a fee entry. Only post_instant_payout_fee_64da22a6 books a fee entry. Skip-run: 7,646.95.
 Four-point test: explicit connective (only after / not until / before ... must); record-visible ledger state; no tool, id or code token; 'every' over the closed set named. All six orders of the three prerequisites were run and give identical values and terminal ledger (the scheduled payout equals the 33,000.00 limit for any payable between 45,284.01 and 46,472.05). The on-demand payout is the seller's own request, confirmed by her in this verified contact.

[Factor card — scheduled payout limit, 5 factors; baseline: payout = min(payable, plan maximum 250,000.00) = 45,325.05]
 new_bank_limit (parameter, multi-source): bank changed 2026-09-25 (20 days), no returned payout -> 0.10 (baseline -> 45,325.05). standing_limit (parameter, cross standing): Top Rated with 430,000.00 -> 1.5 (-> 22,000.00). account_age_limit: 925 days -> 0.8 (-> 41,250.00). fulfillment_limit (cross fulfill): Growth active -> 1.10 (-> 30,000.00). limit_combination (method): chargebacks in six months -> product 0.132 (baseline smallest -> 25,000.00). Result 33,000.00. Near-miss: the profile opened 2024-04-02 is not the payments account date.
[Factor card — won chargeback debit return, 5 factors; baseline: the return basis = lesser of debit 2,860.00 and refunds on the order 1,150.00 = 1,150.00]
 repeat_dispute_fee: 2 disputes in twelve months -> 15.00 (baseline 0 -> 1,150.00). standing_fee_scale (cross standing): Top Rated -> 0.5 (-> 1,144.00). store_fee_scale (cross selling): Premium -> 0.8 (-> 1,146.25). evidence_timing_fee_scale: 1 day -> 0.5 (-> 1,144.00). fee_multiplier_combination (method): account 925 days (>= 730) -> multiplied 0.2 (baseline smallest 0.5 -> 1,142.50). Fee 3.00, result 1,147.00. Near-miss: refund debits on other orders (1,500.00, 2,100.00) are not on the case's order; the lost case CB-20260804-1187 is excluded.
[Factor card — instant fee, 6 factors; baseline: 4,800.00 x plan rate 0.015 = 72.00]
 volume_rate (parameter, multi-source, cross standing): 530,000.00 at Top Rated -> plan rate less 0.0050 = 0.0100 (-> 62.64). pricing_volume_window (method): 925-day account -> larger of 430,000.00 and 2 x 265,000.00 (baseline twelve months -> 0.0125 -> 51.84). store_plan_discount (cross selling) 0.0010 (-> 45.36). frequency_discount: 2 instant payouts in three months -> 0.0005 (-> 43.20). compliance_surcharge (cross standing): 2 points -> 0.0010 (-> 36.72). fulfillment_fee_relief (cross fulfill): Growth -> 0.90 (-> 45.60). Result 41.04. Near-miss: the 2026-08-26 instant payout already carries its 45.00 fee; scheduled payouts are not counted by the frequency tier.
[Factor card — on-demand payout, 6 factors; baseline: payable 13,431.01 after the prerequisites]
 reserve_base_window (method): 925-day account -> larger of the three-month average 50,000.00 and the twelve-month average 35,833.33 (baseline twelve-month -> 8,139.21). surge_reserve_rate (parameter, multi-source, cross standing): Top Rated and surge 1.674 -> 0.05 (-> 9,482.96). fulfillment_reserve_relief (cross fulfill): 1,850 units -> 0.25 (-> 6,982.96). chargeback_holdback_rule: 2 in six months -> 0.5 of net 2,953.00 (-> 9,084.46). refund_holdback_rule: 6.0 percent -> 0.5 (-> 9,407.96). compliance_holdback_rule (cross standing): 2 points -> 0.05 (-> 8,279.51). Result 7,607.96; all-baseline 13,431.01. Near-miss: the 34,800.00 sale credit of 2026-09-02 lies just outside the one-month window.
 Cross-difficulty evidence seeded and read: standing_records (Top Rated Level, good_standing, 2 active violation points), selling_plans (Premium Store, monthly, active; its subscription fees appear as ledger deductions referencing the selling plan's fee records), fulfill_enrollments (FBN Growth Program, active, 1,850 units). Only rows the gold reads are seeded: order rows carry the seller reference and no buyer profile; only the charged-back order's refund record is seeded.

[Base-invariant card] payout_disbursement: account_can_pay — status active; bank_change_hold — anchor 2026-09-25, 3 calendar days on Daily Plus, not_before inclusive: payouts allowed from 2026-09-28; at 2026-10-15 true. payout_instant_terms: no gate. On-demand interval: no earlier on-demand payout on the ledger. payout_chargeback_reversal: dispute_won on CB-20260908-2264 true. payout_instant_fee: policy_scope.
[Business-object card] Scheduled payout: the account's payout of 2026-10-15. Debit return: case CB-20260908-2264 (order of 2026-08-24, 2,860.00) and that order's refund debit 1,150.00 (2026-08-31). Fee: instant payout IP-20261015-527 only. On-demand payout: the account's payable after the three writes.

[World — producible under the charter] 133 ledger rows over 2025-10-16 .. 2026-10-15, simulated day by day: 29 Large Item Freight orders (sale credit, delivery reserve released on delivered date + 3 days, + 3 high-value days at >= 10,000.00), a scheduled payout of the whole payable amount at the cutoff of every business day where it is at least 1.00 (25 payouts; each was recomputed with the scheduled payout limit rule on its own date and equals it), no payout during the 2026-09-25 bank hold (no payable amount existed then: the 2026-09-20 refund debit had left it at -1,500.00 until the 2026-09-27 release, paid 2026-09-28), 12 subscription deductions (two of them took the balance briefly below zero, 2025-11-05..11-13 and 2026-01-05..01-12, cleared by the next sale credit long before the 30 card charge days), 3 seller-funded partial refunds, 2 chargebacks with 15.00 fees, and 2 instant payouts, each taken from the payable amount of its day and within the 5,000.00 daily limit: 2026-08-26 4,000.00 from a payable of 26,300.00 (fee 45.00 priced by the instant fee rule on that day's records) and 2026-10-15 4,800.00 from a payable of 50,125.05 (fee not yet booked). Balance 47,025.05 and reserved 1,700.00 equal the running sums. No automatic clause is left owing.

[Persona] Teodora, brisk owner, asks for an on-demand payout of what is available; volunteers only the request, her name/business and the dashboard impression of about forty-five thousand (true: payable 45,325.05). Verification by phone 5125550412 and tax ID 7231 (ZIP 78704 in reserve). Passive: accepts the figure, asks once why it is lower, submits the payout herself when handed over, reads back the reference, ends. Her only line about prior steps is reactive (only if the agent explains something must be booked first).

[Standard solution / verification] Reads: find_customers(name) -> verify_customer_identity(phone, tax_id_last4) -> find_payments_accounts -> find_payments_ledger -> find_chargeback_disputes -> find_orders(seller) -> find_order_activity(charged-back order) -> find_seller_standing -> find_selling_plans -> find_fbn_enrollments. Writes: send_scheduled_payout 33,000.00; return_won_chargeback_debit (CB-20260908-2264, 1,147.00); post_instant_payout_fee (IP-20261015-527, 41.04); the seller's request_on_demand_payout 7,607.96. The scratch generator replays the gold with the real tools and evaluates every compute through check_compute's evaluator on the handling-time world; outputs equal computations.expected (33000.0, 1147.0, 41.04, 7607.96), the sensitivities above and the baseline results (45325.05, 1150.0, 72.0, 13431.01).

[Draft recomputation from visible context] Daily Plus pays daily -> no 2026-10-15 scheduled payout on the ledger -> the on-demand rule waits -> the scheduled payout rule gives 33,000.00; the disputes show one won case without a return -> 1,147.00; the ledger shows today's instant payout without a fee -> 41.04; then 7,607.96. Matches gold; the six prerequisite orders commute.

[Round 2 — responses by audit item]
 F-1 / T0-1 (window-only method factors): pricing_volume_window now selects, for accounts 365 to 1,094 days old, the larger of two candidate measures (twelve-month credits vs two times six-month credits) — a selection rule, not a window length; reserve_base_window likewise takes the larger of the three-month and twelve-month monthly averages for accounts 730 to 1,094 days old. This task sits on those selection tiers (530,000.00 and 50,000.00). The settlement's refund_window (task 1) became a lower-share comparison between two windows.
 F-2 / T0-2 (unreal item_as_described tier): the evidence_return_basis factor is removed. The return basis is now the baseline method: the case debit, or for a refund_already_issued win the lesser of the debit and the refunds on the same order (the base 'never bears both' sentence made explicit); no tier nets a refund against a won debit any more. The fifth factor is fee_multiplier_combination (method: product / largest / smallest by account age). The base 'never bears both' sentence is now named in overwrite, because a dispute response fee is withheld from such a win (closes O-8). O-7 closed by the rewrite (every compute_basis entry is verbatim).
 F-3 (Enterprise collapse, latent): the volume-priced rates are now the plan rate less 0.0050 / 0.0025, distinct from the plan rate on every plan; the fee-return evidence tiers apply only on plans that do not return the fee on a win. Values here unchanged (Daily Plus: 0.0100 / 0.0125).
 T0-3 (seed contradicted the instant-payout rules): the old 2026-08-27 instant payout (taken from a payable of 0.00) is replaced by a 4,000.00 instant payout on 2026-08-26 from a payable of 26,300.00, and today's instant payout is 4,800.00 (within the 5,000.00 daily limit); the ledger was re-simulated and every scheduled payout re-derived. Consequences: fee 41.04 (was 54.72), on-demand 7,607.96 (was 6,074.96); every figure in this dossier, the traces, the closure and the sensitivities was regenerated.
 O-4 (fee priced on the day's total): no change — latent; the compute and the rule agree whenever one instant payout is dated the fee day, as here (IP-20261015-527 is the only one dated 2026-10-15).
 O-6 / O-T0-c (scheduled excess vs same-day on-demand; new-bank limit): the scheduled rule now says the excess 'is paid by a later payout' and that the payout limit applies to scheduled payouts sent without the seller confirming them in a verified support contact, not to a payout the seller requests and confirms in one — which is this task's on-demand payout.
 O-9 (unstated guards): the on-demand rule now states the surge ratio is 0 with no sale credits in twelve months; the settlement's billing-date test now requires the date to be the settlement day or within 7 days after it.
 O-11 (PPL largest-of-four neutralised the new-bank multiplier): the Preferred Partner tier is now the new-bank multiplier times the largest of the other three.
 O-5, O-10 (settlement): see task 1.
 O-T0-a (persona disposition line): replaced by a purely reactive line. O-T0-b (false near-miss about a skipped 2026-09-25 payout): removed; the world paragraph now states that no payable amount existed during the hold.
user_scenario:
You are Teodora Vasquez-Lind, owner of Lindhaven Commercial Kitchen Supply LLC, a seller on Northloop Marketplace who sells commercial ranges, refrigeration and ovens to restaurants. You are calling the Northloop seller support desk on Thursday late morning from your warehouse office; you are brisk and organised, speak in short practical sentences, and you are under some time pressure because a supplier wants a deposit before the weekend.

What you want: you would like to take an on-demand payout today of the money that is available on your Northloop Payments account, sent to the bank account you have on file. You do not have a figure in mind beyond "what is available"; when you glanced at your dashboard this morning the available amount looked to be somewhere around forty-five thousand dollars, but you know dashboards are not always the final word and you want whatever the desk says can actually go out today.

You know you have to confirm the payout yourself, so when the agent says the on-demand payout is ready for you to submit and hands it over to you, you submit it yourself with the payments account reference and the amount the agent gives you, and you read back the payout reference you get. Only if the agent explains that something has to be booked or settled on the account first do you react to it: you then simply say that is fine and to go ahead, and you do not ask for details of it.

To identify yourself: your name is Teodora Vasquez-Lind and the business is Lindhaven Commercial Kitchen Supply LLC. When the agent asks for verification details, you give your mobile number 5125550412 and the last four digits of your business tax ID, 7231. If they ask for something else, you also know your billing ZIP code is 78704. You do not know any internal reference numbers by heart.

Only if the agent asks which bank account the payout should go to, you say the one currently on file, ending 3381. Only if the agent asks whether you want an instant payout to your card instead, you say no, a regular on-demand payout to the bank is what you want. If the agent asks how much you want, you say whatever is available to go out today.

When the agent tells you the amount that can go out on demand, you accept it. If it is far below what you saw on the dashboard, you ask once, politely, why it is lower than the roughly forty-five thousand you saw this morning, listen to the explanation, and accept it without arguing about figures. You never suggest any figure, rule or step yourself.

Once you have submitted the payout and read back the payout reference, you thank the agent and say goodbye; you have nothing else to raise.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The three prerequisite writes are parallel and commute. All six orders were run: every order gives scheduled payout 33,000.00, returned debit 1,147.00, instant fee 41.04 and on-demand payout 7,607.96, and the same terminal ledger. Reason: the scheduled payout equals the payout limit 33,000.00, which binds for any payable amount between 45,284.01 and 46,472.05; the debit return reads only the dispute, the case debit, the order's refund debits, the account age and other categories; the fee reads only sale credits, instant payout counts and other categories. No shared balance cap or dedup key ties them.

Skipping the instant fee leaves the payable at 13,472.05; the compliance holdback becomes 673.60 and the on-demand payout 7,646.95 instead of 7,607.96 (and the terminal ledger lacks the 41.04 fee entry).
